ctx.x: He was my cousin on my mother's side. I only met one of my father's relatives, and that was when I was with Cab Calloway when we played in Haiti, and I met one of my cousins who was a Senator there at the time.

items.title: Panama Francis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: Later gigs with Billy Hicks, Roy Eldridge, Lucky Millinder and Cab Calloway made him a familiar and sought-after drummer

ctx.x: Drummer David “Panama” Francis has been performing professionally since the 1930’s. A native of Miami, David played his first engagements with the Florida Collegians and in New York with Tab Smith. Later gigs with Billy Hicks, Roy Eldridge, Lucky Millinder and Cab Calloway made him a familiar and sought-after drummer for both recordings and live shows. items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Oh, he was a character if there ever was one; Freddie the Freeloader.

ctx.x: Freddie the Freeloader! He was a character.
Oh, he was a character if there ever was one; Freddie the Freeloader.
Oh, he'd bring my bass in on a date and he'd sit there and he'd have a few tastes -- he'd be the first one at the bar; before you ordered yours, he had already ordered and he said it was on you.
